scenes.tts: Every protein in the nucleus was made in the cytoplasm. Histones, polymerases and transcription factors all have to be brought in. The border is busy in both directions at once. So how does the nucleus collect the right proteins, keep them, and make traffic run one way?
scenes.visual: Cytoplasm with proteins, an unknown box in the nucleus, a two-headed question arrow at the pore, then one arrow with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Every protein in the nucleus was made in the cytoplasm. Histones, polymerases and transcription factors all have to be brought in. The border is busy in both directions at once. So how does the nucleus collect the right proteins, keep them, and make traffic run one way?

scenes.tts: The gates in this border are nuclear pore complexes. Anyone small can stroll across. A large protein needs a passport, a short signal called a nuclear localization signal. A courier called importin alpha reads it. Importin beta binds importin alpha, then moves the complex through the pore by binding F G repeats.

scenes.visual: Small dots pass the pore freely; a large cargo waits; a signal tag, importin alpha and importin beta join it and it slides through the FG repeats.
scenes.narration: The gates in this border are nuclear pore complexes. Anyone small can stroll across. A large protein needs a passport, a short signal called a nuclear localization signal. scenes.tts: The pore does not set the direction. The couriers do not push anyone through. What makes traffic one way is a rule about where couriers put their loads down. That rule depends on Ran, a small G T P ase. Ran is on with G T P and off with G D P.

scenes.visual: Crossed-out push arrow; a courier puts its load down; Ran GTP (on) and Ran GDP (off) chips swap.
scenes.narration: The pore does not set the direction. The couriers do not push anyone through. What makes traffic one way is a rule about where couriers put their loads down. That rule depends on Ran, a small GTPase. Ran is on with GTP and off with GDP.

scenes.tts: In the nucleus, an exchange factor called R C C one sits on chromatin and loads G T P onto Ran. So Ran G T P is made in the nucleus. In the cytoplasm, R a n G A P one makes Ran break down its G T P, so cytoplasmic Ran G T P stays low. A carrier called N T F two brings Ran G D P back into the nucleus to be recharged.
scenes.caption: In the nucleus, an exchange factor called RCC1 sits on chromatin and loads GTP onto Ran. So RanGTP is made in the nucleus. In the cytoplasm, RanGAP1 makes Ran break down its GTP, so cytoplasmic RanGTP stays low. A carrier called NTF2 brings RanGDP back into the nucleus to be recharged.
scenes.visual: Green RanGTP dots fill the nucleus from RCC1 on chromatin; in the cytoplasm RanGAP1 turns green to red; NTF2 carries a red dot in, and it turns green.
scenes.narration: In the nucleus, an exchange factor called RCC1 sits on chromatin and loads GTP onto Ran. So RanGTP is made in the nucleus. In the cytoplasm, RanGAP1 makes Ran break down its GTP, so cytoplasmic RanGTP stays low. A carrier called NTF2 brings RanGDP back into the nucleus to be recharged.

scenes.tts: The couriers read this gradient. An importin loads cargo where Ran G T P is low, then drops it when Ran G T P binds in the nucleus. An exportin such as C R M one does the opposite. It binds its cargo only together with Ran G T P. In the cytoplasm, hydrolysis breaks the complex apart.
scenes.caption: The couriers read this gradient. An importin loads cargo where RanGTP is low, then drops it when RanGTP binds in the nucleus. An exportin such as CRM1 does the opposite. It binds its cargo only together with RanGTP. In the cytoplasm, hydrolysis breaks the complex apart.
scenes.visual: Importin carries cargo in and drops it when RanGTP binds; CRM1 with RanGTP carries cargo out and drops it when the GTP is hydrolysed.
scenes.narration: The couriers read this gradient. An importin loads cargo where RanGTP is low, then drops it when RanGTP binds in the nucleus. An exportin such as CRM1 does the opposite. It binds its cargo only together with RanGTP. In the cytoplasm, hydrolysis breaks the complex apart.

scenes.tts: Where is the energy spent? Not on pushing. In a test tube assay, transportin, another importin, carried cargo across pores with no Ran or nucleotide present. G T P hydrolysis builds and resets the gradient that decides where loads are picked up and dropped. Keep this rule: the pore is open, and Ran G T P sets the direction.
